messages.subject: Founder effects (coef) help
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I am trying to determine founder effects in a cohort of diversity outbred mice and can't work out why I'm getting such high QTL effects (image attached). I wondered whether you had come across this before or knew what might be causing it?

The code used to generate the image is also attached. Please let me know if you need any other information.

Kind regards,

Harry

```{r}

fapr <- fst_genoprob(apr, "apr", tmpdir, overwrite = TRUE)

k <- calc_kinship(fapr, type = "loco", cores = 6, quiet = FALSE)

coef <- scan1coef(fapr[ , "2"], DO$pheno[ , 1], k[["2"]])

par(mar=c(4.1, 4.1, 0.6, 0.6))
plot_coefCC(coef, DO$pmap, legend = "bottomleft")

```

messages.body_plain:
When one or more of the founder alleles is absent, the corresponding coefficient can't be estimated. It should be NA, but it's difficult to ensure that happens.

You can try using the function clean_genoprob() to set small probabilities to 0, and then run scan1coef() again.

But that still may not solve the problem. I'd mostly recommend focusing on particular locations of interest (such as the location of an inferred QTL) and just getting the estimated effects at such specific locations.

karl

messages.body_plain:
The R/qtl2 User Guide, in the section on SNP association, points to the resource we've made available, with genotypes for the Collaborative Cross founders:

    https://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/vignettes/user_guide.html#connecting_to_snp_and_gene_databases

Namely, there's a SQLite database on Figshare:

    https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.5280229.v3

The user guide no longer talks about how to use genoprob_to_snprob(), as we're expecting that most people would just want to call scan1snps() and not bother with the detailed steps. But basically you need to:

  - use create_variant_query_func() to connect to the snp database
  - call the created function to grab SNP genotypes for some desired region, which could be a whole chromosome
  - call genoprob_to_snpprob() with your genotype or allele probabilities plus the SNP table

karl

messages.body_plain:
genoprob_to_snpprob() uses the genotype probabilities plus genotypes on the founder strains to effectively impute SNP genotypes in the DO mice.
So while you've got genotype data at 4711 variants, the 8 founders have been genotyped at 49,981 variants, and genoprob_to_snpprob() is calculating SNP genotype probabilities at that larger set of variants.

To save effort, it bins SNPs by the pattern of alleles in the founder strains, and by the interval between genotyped markers. The 49,981 SNPs are apparently mostly sitting in intervals between the 4711 variants, but a few are at the same position as those 4711 variants.

karl

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] VCF
messages.body_plain:
The genotypes need to be coded in the same way for all markers, for example A/B or AA/BB.
Heterozygotes will be omitted.

An example of recombinant inbred lines is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rqtl/qtl2data/master/BXD/

You need not just the genotype data and the yaml file but also a genetic map of the markers.

For RIL derived from two founders, you could also arrange the data to be read into R/qtl1, read them in with read.cross() from the R/qtl1 package, and then use convert2cross2() in R/qtl2 to convert the dataset into the R/qtl2 "cross2" object format.

karl

messages.body_plain:
R version 4 was released at https://cran.r-project.org.

I've built R/qtl2 binaries for R v4. When you upgrade R, update your R/qtl2 packages:

  update.packages(repos="https://rqtl.org/qtl2cran", ask=FALSE, checkBuilt=TRUE)

Or install again from scratch:

  install.packages("qtl2", repos="https://rqtl.org/qtl2cran")

karl
